findings.headline: 6 of 6 documented 99215 claims were documented below the billed level
findings.interpretation: 99215 on 27.8% of claims vs 2.6% expected (z_adj 9.64); 45% of 99215s were for patients with 0–1 chronic conditions. Random sample of 30 charts: 12 (40%) were below the billed level. Draft overpayment estimate from the random sample is $3,864 (CI $3,232–4,495). Needs coder re-scoring before any action.

findings.headline: 5 of 6 documented 99215 claims were documented below the billed level
findings.interpretation: 99215 on 31.5% vs 3.5% expected (z_adj 9.15); 42% of 99215s were for low-complexity patients. Charts became usable after the office added signatures. 6 of 30 random charts were below the billed level. Draft overpayment estimate is $2,999 (CI $1,880–4,117). Needs human review.

findings.headline: 5 of 11 documented 99215 claims (46%) were below the billed level, vs 9% for peers
findings.interpretation: The panel is genuinely sick: only 6% of 99215s were for low-complexity patients. But the 99215 share is 45% vs 8% expected (z_adj 8.36), and charts show moderate or low MDM on many 99215s. 8 of 30 random charts were below the billed level. Draft overpayment estimate is $2,854 (CI $1,422–4,286). The acuity explains part of the excess, not all of it.

findings.headline: Highest risk-adjusted 99215 rate on a healthy panel, but the notes support the billed levels
findings.interpretation: 30% 99215 vs 2% expected (z_adj 12.0); 71% of 99215s were for patients with 0–1 conditions (URI, UTI, back pain). The 24 legible charts nominally support the billed levels (1 below billed). However, 4 of 19 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review had no lab or test on the claim (17%), so the notes may be inflated to match the bill. Top priority for a certified coder to re-score the notes independently. Not referred for recovery on current evidence.

findings.headline: Largest excess 99215 volume (about 307 claims); documentation supports the billing
findings.interpretation: z_adj 12.6 on 2,108 claims, elevated in every complexity group. 30 random charts: only 1 below billed and 2 of 19 notes with data review but no tests on the claim. Charts do not support upcoding. The pattern could reflect thorough documentation or note inflation; a coder should spot-check it.

findings.headline: 99215 share is high in every complexity group; 30 of 30 charts support the billed level
findings.interpretation: z_adj 10.0. 0 of 30 random charts were below billed, and 2 of 21 notes had data review with no tests on the claim. The claims pattern is concerning, but the chart evidence does not support upcoding.
